newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish police bar foreign bikers from gang funeral.
newsitem.headline: Danish police bar foreign bikers from gang funeral.

text.p: Denmark closed its borders to foreign bikers on Thursday in a bid to head off possible violence at the funeral of a motorcycle gang member.

Danish police said border checks had been tightened and surveillance points set up around Torup Church, 50 km (30 miles) north of Copenhagen, where the funeral was to take place on Thursday afternoon.
Newspapers reported that a Swedish motorcycle gang member had been turned back by Danish customs officers at the port of Elsinore, north of Copenhagen.

"We have sent warnings out to the local Torup population to prevent them from inadvertently getting involved in any conflict that might flare up between rival biker gangs," police inspector Kaj Knudsen told the Danish national news agency Ritzau.

In the latest clash in a simmering Nordic biker war that has now taken 10 lives, assailants believed to be members of the Hells Angels motorcycle gang shot dead a member of the rival Bandidos and wounded three others in a Danish seaside town on June 7.

The shooting took place only days after a Bandidos clubhouse in the Norwegian town of Drammen was attacked by a car bomb that killed a woman passer-by, prompting Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland to promise a crackdown on the Nordic offshoots of U.S. motorcycle clans.
There has been bitter rivalry between the two gangs since the Bandidos first began to challenge Hells Angels' dominance of the Nordic region in 1993.
